title: Solo embedding incident log — dimensional mismatch & latency
content:
Summary:
Observed two related anomalies on the embeddings + rerank path during production traffic window 2026-03-09 18:00–19:30 UTC: (1) sporadic embedding dimension mismatch errors causing rerank API 400s (~0.4% of requests in window) and (2) correlated latency spikes on the rerank endpoint (p95 from ~120ms -> 850ms). Both started after a staggered SDK rollout (client-sdk v1.12.0 -> v1.12.1) on 2026-03-09 17:45 UTC.

Symptoms / error snippets observed:
- Error returned by rerank service: "400 Bad Request: embedding vector length mismatch — expected 1536, got 1024"
- Consumer logs (python SDK) show: "embedding() returned len=1024 for model open-embedding-small-v2"
- Rerank service log around spike: "rerank: waiting for fallback embeddings; blocking 12 reqs; kv-cache miss; compute queue length 18"
- GPU memory/alloc spikes on dedicated pool host-12 around 18:03 UTC (+30% transient)

Timeline (rough):
- 17:40 UTC: canary of client-sdk v1.12.1 to 2% of traffic (internal CI signal green)
- 17:45–18:00 UTC: rollout to 25% — first 1024-dim error reported by a customer (ticket RINF-1243 opened)
- 18:00–18:30 UTC: progressively larger fraction saw errors; p95 latency for rerank jumps; team telemetry showed more cache misses and repeated model fallback attempts
- 18:40 UTC: rollback of SDK rollout to 0% -> errors drop to baseline within ~6 minutes

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Local Python repro (client-sdk v1.12.1):
   - pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/client-sdk@v1.12.1
   - python snippet:

     from redwood import Embeddings, RerankClient
     emb = Embeddings(model='open-embedding-small-v2')
     vec = emb.embed(['short text'])
     print(len(vec[0]))  # -> 1024 in failing build

2) Curl to rerank endpoint with 1024-length vector (simulating client):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/rerank \ 
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
     -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["a","b"],"embeddings":[[...1024 floats...]]}'
   -> 400, message about expected 1536

Local instrumentation commands used:
- kubectl logs -n dedicated svc/rerank --since=2h | grep "embedding vector length"
- ngrep/tcpdump on host-12 to inspect payloads (sampled)
- traced GPU allocs via nvidia-smi/pmon during repro window

Hypotheses (ordered by my subjective likelihood):
A) SDK regression: client-sdk v1.12.1 defaulted to model variant "open-embedding-small-v2" which changed embedding size to 1024 in its internal mapping (packaged default mapping mismatch). This leads clients to send 1024-length vectors while rerank expects 1536 from the canonical model in service config. (High)
B) Model aliasing mismatch in runtime routing: the serving routing table for "open-embedding-small" was updated to point to a 1024-dim quantized variant for cost reasons, but rerank service's input validation still expects 1536. This would cause server-side rejects for some routed requests. (Medium)
C) Truncation bug in serialization path: proto/js -> bytes converter dropped trailing dims under high concurrency, producing shorter vectors on the wire. Would explain intermittent nature and coupling with high qps. (Low)
D) KV-cache/aggregation bug: older cached prefixes were stored with 1024 vectors from an older config and used in rerank computation leading to shape mismatch during mixed-model compute. (Low)

Observations supporting A:
- All failing clients had the same client-sdk version in request metadata (x-client-version header)
- Rolling back client rollout eliminated new errors almost immediately
- In local reproducer using v1.12.1 I reliably see 1024 output

Observations supporting B/C/D:
- GPU alloc spikes and queueing correlate to the same window, suggesting server attempts to fallback or reencode in some requests
- Some customer logs show "model fallback -> quantized-1024-v3" which correlates to B

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Blocklisted client-sdk v1.12.1 in gateway at 18:40 UTC (fast rollback) -> error rate returned to baseline
- Added temporary validation at gateway to reject non-1536 vectors with clearer log message and a focused metric for easy alerting (metric: rerank.input.shape.invalid.count)

Next steps (short term):
- Confirm mapping table used by client-sdk v1.12.1 for model name -> embedding size (Devon to dump wheel and check mapping)
- Add a strict assertion in the SDK that verifies model->dim mapping at import time and fails loudly in alpha builds (me)
- Create lightweight infra check that compares serving model manifest (catalog) with rerank expected dims and alerts on mismatch (SRE)
- Repro and instrument serialization path: enable pcap capture for one failing customer session and compare payload lengths (me + Devon)
- Review PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/782 for recent input validation changes (linked)

Longer-term actions:
- Add end-to-end compatibility test (client-sdk x runtime manifest) into CI gating to catch model alias/dim mismatch before rollout
- Strengthen API contract: accept vector dimension in request envelope and return a standard well-documented error code with remediation steps (client-side SDK upgrade note)
- Investigate why rerank p95 spikes when dimension errors occur — likely retry/backoff and synchronous fallback causing queue buildup; move heavy fallback work off fast path

Things I still need to check / open questions:
- Does any other model name mapping in v1.12.1 default to new dims? (search wheel for mapping dict)
- Were there two independent changes (client mapping + serving routing) that coincided by accident?
- Could quantization profiles be changing dims (e.g., latent compression to 1024) or is that a renaming artifact?

Quick commands I ran during a rapid triage (copyable):
- pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/client-sdk@v1.12.1 && python -c "from redwood import Embeddings; print(len(Embeddings(model='open-embedding-small-v2').embed(['x'])[0]))"
- kubectl -n dedicated exec -it deploy/rerank -- bash -c "jq '.models' /etc/redwood/manifest.json"
- curl -s -H 'x-client-version: client-sdk/1.12.1' https://internal-metrics.redwood/api/trace?trace_id=abc123 | jq '.events[] | select(.msg|test("embedding"))'

Notes to self: keep this as a step-by-step incident breadcrumb for postmortem. Write a short postmortem once root cause confirmed. Leave the temporary gateway check in place for 48h and roll out a fix via CI-only canary to avoid client-caused waves.

Signed: Anika

-- End of scratchpad --
